answer: A farm running 23 keys therefore pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation cheap. Because the falcon stake is held until the terrace settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the nadir audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 42% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a cheap one. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
